label: read-bm-science
in_my_words: They want to know if a 3D printer can make plastic strips made of two layers that curl up when the air gets damp, like a pine cone scale opening. They use an old formula, with one piece of it confirmed by a computer, to throw out hopeless designs before printing anything. They have not printed a strip yet.
how_in_my_words: They take a 1925 formula for how much a two-layer strip bends and have a proof-checking program confirm it can never exceed 1.5 times the mismatch over the thickness. They test the checker with bad proofs, compare the formula to a computer simulation, and gather pine cone numbers. They estimate how fast water would soak into printing plastics. Then they cross off designs that the limit or the slow soaking rules out. The last step, printing and measuring real strips, is still to do.

test_questions.question: What is the maximum curl the formula allows?
test_questions.my_answer: 1.5 times the size mismatch divided by the thickness.

test_questions.question: Is the limit a new discovery?
test_questions.my_answer: No, it was plotted in 2015; the new part is the computer proof.

test_questions.question: What result would show they are wrong?
test_questions.my_answer: A real printed strip curling tighter than the limit, or a half-thickness layer not being much faster.

test_questions.question: Has any strip been printed and measured?
test_questions.my_answer: No, that step is still to do.

test_questions.question: What exactly is the size mismatch measured in?
test_questions.my_answer: Unclear; the text only says how much more one layer swells than the other.

sentences_i_could_not_follow: The formula says the stiffness ratio drops out once the layers are the best thickness.
It over-predicts the tightest bend of printed soft humidity strips by about four times.
A grid maximum of 1.5000000000000002, and a time constant of 0.7239 for curvature.
It also rejected a false version that said 7/5 instead of 3/2.
The formula is for a thin ribbon, and a wide sheet behaves differently, rolling up about 30 to 50 percent tighter in one direction only.
what_would_help: Say once, concretely, what mismatch and thickness numbers a real strip would have, and what curl radius results. Cut the long list of caveats and technical details, and explain the stiffness-ratio point simply.
